195eced229: As my partner Bob Buchholz was spray painting over some gang tags on the outer front wall of our apartment building, our landlord Tom Nizinski was walking by with his dog. Tom asked Bob, "Would Diane like to do a mural?" When Bob relayed the invitation to paint the building I was electrified with enthusiasm! Seemed like a win/win opportunity to me and the building owners! Our landlords covered the cost of paint. I gave them a few watercolor painting designs from which to choose preferences, and Bob helped me with chalk lining, grid drawing, priming, measuring and helping out with the ladder. I painted in all the details. It was a great relief to have such a monumental creative endeavor happening on such a great scale in our own neighborhood, on our own dwelling place during the pandemic! And where there is art...there are no gang tags. That's the long known "law" among the gangs. "More Art Less Tags" we say! There is also a shrine in the doorway by my partner, Robert Buchholz. His artwork is primarily found object assemblages.

(Photo Credit: Sandra Steinbrecher) Ruben Aguirre is a Chicago-based painter who has transitioned from graffiti writing to an abstract/contemporary muralist.
While working on this project Aguirre stated, “The first inspiration is the space itself. My work is a response to a site specific place, so looking, thinking and reacting with paint is the result of being there.” – as quoted in Sandra Steinbrecher’s Wabash Arts Corridor / Big Walls / 2016

1a8e5f9289: The memorial wall is celebrating the life and contributions of four Puerto Rican, artists, poets, activist and trail blazers in the arts and literary world. The homage to these poets, artist and activist is to bring to the public an awareness of their artistic legacy and give them recognition for their journey in using the spoken word and brush to paint with pride and dignity so future generations will stand strong and be proud of their cultural ties. Featured from left to right Legend pioneers, Salima Rivera (1946-2004) David Hernandez (1946-2013) Gamaliel Ramirez (1949-2018) and Julia De Burgos (1914-1953) - The wall features black and white images of these Puerto Ricans with excerpts of their poetry in proximity of their image along with shadow images of icons relevant to their character. The span of the background of the mural is of the Puerto Rican Flag. Assistant Artist – John Pitman Weber, Patricia Perez and Alisa Scott
